subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: HER2-positive breast cancer: targeted therapy and cardiac safety

steps.tx: HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor 2) is a growth receptor that, when present in excess, pushes breast tumours towards more aggressive behaviour. **Trastuzumab** is a monoclonal antibody aimed at HER2 and forms the core of treatment. Its chief dose-limiting adverse effect is **cardiotoxicity**, so heart function, usually tracked through **left ventricular ejection fraction** (LVEF) monitoring, must be followed throughout therapy. **Pertuzumab** adds a second layer of HER2 blockade on top of trastuzumab.

steps.tx: Cardiac surveillance is central to anti-HER2 therapy. Assess **LVEF** (left ventricular ejection fraction) by echocardiography or MUGA before starting, then repeat it at regular intervals, typically every 3 months during treatment for dual blockade and trastuzumab-based regimens. A fall in LVEF below the protocol threshold requires holding the drug and reassessing. Indian practice follows the same principle, so monitoring should not be skipped in resource-limited centres.

steps.tx: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), studied in **KATHERINE**, is an antibody-drug conjugate used as adjuvant therapy in patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and trastuzumab. Thrombocytopenia is a key haematologic toxicity. For grade 3 or 4 platelet falls, hold the drug until recovery to grade 1 or better, then resume according to protocol dose modification. Hepatotoxicity also needs regular liver function monitoring.

steps.tx: Neoadjuvant therapy aims for a **pathological complete response** (pCR), meaning no invasive cancer left in breast or nodes. pCR predicts better survival, especially in HER2-positive and triple-negative disease. The APHINITY trial showed that adding pertuzumab to adjuvant trastuzumab improved invasive disease-free survival in early HER2-positive breast cancer. Residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy identifies patients who need intensified adjuvant treatment.
